physics.solver: Genesis 1.4.3 + libuipc 0.0.29, IPC contact, FEM shell/volume
physics.grasp_model: finite-force finger PD and IPC friction, no ideal attachment
physics.rigid_contact_solver: Genesis rigid solver with scene-local restoration of IPC-delegated collision pairs
physics.soft_environment_contact: tabletop, legs, mounts and floor participate in native IPC contact
physics.bear_material_scope: homogeneous compressible elastic filling approximation; no separate textile skin
physics.bag_material_scope: two cloth panels sewn on three edges; thin shell with separate effective stretch, shear and bending stiffness; no yarn model
physics.cloth_thickness_convention: IPC thickness is a radius; physical thickness is twice the configured value

initialization.method: Actual qpos after rigid solver build, before IPC geometry build

shell_conversion.scope: Per-scene pre-initialization FEM shell coefficient conversion
shell_conversion.thickness_semantics: IPC one-sided radius r; full thickness h=2r

stc_reaction_feedback.method: Exact native STC energy gradient, rigid-target virtual work
stc_reaction_feedback.wrench_reference: world axes, torque about target link origin

rigid_contact_pairing.method: Scene-local Collider subclass; original Genesis pair filters with temporary delegation tags hidden

policy.note: Lateral/overlap/perimeter are declared trial policies, not physical laws. Explicit lateral/overlap values permit a bounded contact experiment, not a material-feasibility claim. The initial COM search radius does not change the 30 mm individual or 50 mm cumulative correction budget. The 5 mm minimum teddy/left-robot clearance is an engineering preflight allowance, not a physical law. Bottom clearance and lateral trial fraction are configurable; no compression is prescribed.

geometry_guarantees: Uses the ordered actual 3D body rim, not a fitted mouth plane.
The observed teddy is translated without imposed compression or rotation.
Thin-slab convex envelopes enclose every horizontal section between tetra vertex-height events.
Whole observed teddy begins above highest rim by at least 40 mm and ends below lowest rim by 2 mm, with configured table clearance.
Every preparation and insertion segment's complete frozen-shape teddy translation must clear every left robot collision volume by the declared engineering allowance.
Robot path retains analytic continuous joint-limit and sampled 8 mm rigid-clearance checks.
not_guaranteed: Deformable 3D bag interior containment or passage under contact.
Frictional grasp retention, force/torque, cloth strain or tetrahedron quality during execution.
A nonplanar rim can contact several teddy heights simultaneously; independent section guards do not certify that coupled contact.
Cartesian frozen-shape sweep certificates do not predict deformation or prove continuous FK tracking; sampled FK position/orientation errors are reported separately.
Overlap fraction is a bounded trial heuristic for slab envelopes, not an exact occupied-section or continuous-contact theorem.
Saved observations lack native contact force/torque; runtime guards and final containment audit are mandatory.

topology.body_face_selection: explicit physical body-face labels mapped to imported rest mesh

left_robot_teddy_sweep.model_scope: continuous frozen tetrahedral body versus MuJoCo convex collision solids
limitations: Does not predict deformation, friction, grasp retention or contact forces.
Robot convex envelopes can overestimate nonconvex native collision surfaces.
Left pose is fixed at measured q; native affine compliance and future tracking are not included.
Only the declared straight translation segment is certified; other segments and obstacles require separate gates.
The certificate is for frozen-shape Cartesian translation, not continuous FK tracking of an interpolated joint trajectory.
A fresh actual-shape check remains necessary after physical preparation.

contact_guard.scope: Exact STC feedback from native IPC soft contacts only; excludes Genesis rigid-contact forces
contact_guard.force_links: right link7 (includes welded palm) plus both fingers
contact_guard.torque_reference: aim TCP in world axes; link-origin moments shifted by cross(origin-TCP,F)
contact_guard.diagnostics: Per-link right aim origins and shifted moments; all left-arm cached raw wrenches/origins and moments about the left aim TCP. No added force/torque thresholds.
limitations: Opening reactions do not identify the contacted soft material; the named handle material-group proximity guard is also required.
Net force can cancel opposing loads; per-finger norms, torque, soft strain, grip, and rigid-collision guards remain necessary.
A baseline is recorded for diagnosis; thresholds always apply to raw values.
